institutions.name: University of Bologna
institutions.summary: The oldest university of the Latin West, grown from the law teaching of Irnerius and the glossators around 1100. Its student-run 'universitates' of jurists became the model for southern European universities, and it remained a leading centre of Roman and canon law, medicine and natural philosophy.
institutions.notes: 1088 is a conventional date fixed by an 1888 commission (Carducci); law teaching is securely attested only from c. 1100–1120.

institutions.name: Studium of Vicenza
institutions.summary: Short-lived studium formed by masters and students who left Bologna in 1204. It is the first documented Bolognese secession and illustrates how mobile the early law schools were.
institutions.notes: Ceased within a few years, by c. 1209–1210; masters largely returned to Bologna.

institutions.name: Studium of Arezzo
institutions.summary: Studium begun when the jurist Roffredo of Benevento and others left Bologna for Arezzo around 1215. It received statutes in 1255 and an imperial charter in 1355 but faded in the later 14th century.
institutions.notes: End date conventional: the studium had effectively ceased by the time Florence acquired Arezzo in 1384.

institutions.name: University of Padua
institutions.summary: Founded by students and masters who left Bologna in 1222, Padua became the university of the Venetian Republic and a magnet for foreign students. Its tolerance and medical school (Vesalius, Fabricius, Harvey, Galileo) made it a leading centre of the Scientific Revolution.

institutions.name: Studium of Vercelli
institutions.summary: Studium set up in 1228 under a contract between the commune of Vercelli and students seceding from Padua. It taught law and arts intermittently and faded in the 14th century.
institutions.notes: The 1228 contract survives; the end is uncertain, with the studium inactive by the mid-14th century.

institutions.name: University of Siena
institutions.summary: Municipal studium documented from 1240, strengthened by a Bolognese secession in 1321 and an imperial charter of 1357. It remained a mid-sized law and medicine university under Siena and later the Medici grand dukes.

institutions.name: University of Naples
institutions.summary: Founded by Frederick II in 1224 as the first state university, to train jurists and officials for the Kingdom of Sicily independently of the papacy. It remained the only university of the mainland Kingdom of Naples until the 19th century.
institutions.notes: The move to Salerno under Conrad IV and return under Manfred is commonly reported but poorly documented.

institutions.name: Schola Medica Salernitana
institutions.summary: The earliest medical school of medieval Europe, flourishing from the 10th–12th centuries and transmitting Greek and Arabic medicine through Constantine the African's translations. It remained a medical faculty with degree-granting rights until Murat suppressed it in 1811.
institutions.notes: Origins are legendary; physicians of Salerno are attested from the mid-10th century.

institutions.name: Studium Urbis (La Sapienza)
institutions.summary: Founded by Boniface VIII in 1303 as the city's university, distinct from the Studium Curiae. Reorganised by Eugenius IV and housed in the Sapienza palace, it became the Italian state's university of the capital after 1870.

institutions.name: Studium Curiae
institutions.summary: Studium generale attached to the papal court, created by Innocent IV and following the curia on its travels. It taught theology and law to curial clergy and was later merged into the city university of Rome.
institutions.notes: The curia was itinerant in central Italy after 1251 (Perugia, Viterbo, Orvieto, Anagni); 'Rome' stands for that phase. The date of its absorption by the Studium Urbis is uncertain.

institutions.name: Collegio Romano
institutions.summary: Founded by Ignatius of Loyola in 1551 as the flagship Jesuit college, it set the curriculum of the Ratio Studiorum and was a centre of mathematics and astronomy (Clavius, Kircher, Secchi). Expelled from its building by the Italian state in 1873, it continued as the Pontifical Gregorian University.
institutions.notes: Received degree-granting powers from the papacy in 1556; classed here as Jesuit college.

institutions.name: Collegio Urbano de Propaganda Fide
institutions.summary: Missionary seminary-college founded by Urban VIII to train clergy for the missions, with degree-granting rights in philosophy and theology.

institutions.name: University of Perugia
institutions.summary: A communal law school raised to studium generale by Clement V in 1308. In the 14th century it was the seat of Bartolus and Baldus, the most influential commentators on Roman law.
institutions.notes: The commune had paid teachers since c. 1276.

institutions.name: Studium of Treviso
institutions.summary: Studium generale chartered by Frederick the Fair in 1318 at the request of the commune. It had little sustained activity.
institutions.notes: Largely a paper foundation; end date conventional.

institutions.name: University of Pisa
institutions.summary: Founded by papal bull in 1343, Pisa became the university of the Florentine state after Lorenzo de' Medici's refoundation in 1473 and Cosimo I's in 1543. Galileo studied and taught there, and it was a major scientific centre in the 19th century.
institutions.notes: During the Pisan revolt (1494–1509) the studio moved among Florence, Prato and Pistoia; dates of the moves are approximate.

institutions.name: Studio Fiorentino
institutions.summary: The commune of Florence's studium, chartered by the pope and emperor in the 14th century. It became the leading centre of Greek studies and humanism (Chrysoloras, Argyropoulos) before Lorenzo de' Medici transferred it to Pisa.
institutions.notes: After 1473 some humanities chairs (e.g. Poliziano's) remained in Florence.

institutions.name: Istituto di Studi Superiori Pratici e di Perfezionamento
institutions.summary: Advanced institute created by the Tuscan provisional government, with sections of letters/philosophy, medicine and natural sciences. It awarded degrees and became the University of Florence in 1924.

institutions.name: Scuola Normale Superiore
institutions.summary: Founded by Napoleon as a Pisan branch of the École normale of Paris to train teachers. Refounded by Leopold II in 1846, it became the elite teacher-training school of united Italy.
institutions.notes: Opened 1813; closed 1814; refounded 1846, reopened 1847.

institutions.name: University of Pavia
institutions.summary: Founded with an imperial charter for Galeazzo II Visconti in 1361, Pavia was the university of the Duchy of Milan. Its Theresian reform made it a model Enlightenment university with Volta and Spallanzani.
institutions.notes: The transfer to Piacenza (1398–c.1412) was partial; dates approximate.

institutions.name: Studium of Piacenza
institutions.summary: Paper studium generale granted to Piacenza by Innocent IV in 1248. It saw little activity, though the Visconti later moved the Pavia studium there (1398–1412).
institutions.notes: End date conventional.

institutions.name: Studium of Reggio Emilia
institutions.summary: Law studium active in Reggio from the late 12th century, staffed partly by Bolognese masters. It flourished in the 13th century before disappearing.
institutions.notes: Both start and end are approximate.

institutions.name: University of Modena
institutions.summary: Law studium begun when Pillius of Medicina left Bologna for Modena in the 1180s. Revived by the Este dukes as a public university in 1682 and reformed in 1772.
institutions.notes: Continuity between the medieval studium and the 1682 foundation is disputed.

institutions.name: University of Parma
institutions.summary: Studium generale established by Niccolò III d'Este in 1412, refounded by Ranuccio I Farnese in 1601 and reformed by the Bourbon minister Du Tillot in 1768.
institutions.notes: Episcopal and law schools existed in Parma from the 10th–13th centuries; the University claims 962.

institutions.name: University of Ferrara
institutions.summary: Founded by bull of Boniface IX in 1391 at the request of Alberto V d'Este and revived in 1442. A humanist and medical centre where Copernicus took his doctorate.

institutions.name: Studium of Verona
institutions.summary: Paper studium generale granted to Verona by Benedict XII in 1339; little evidence of activity.

institutions.name: Studium of Cividale
institutions.summary: Imperial paper foundation for Cividale del Friuli by Charles IV; it never functioned as a university.

institutions.name: Studium of Lucca
institutions.summary: Imperial charter for a studium generale granted to Lucca by Charles IV in 1369; it remained essentially a paper foundation.

institutions.name: University of Turin
institutions.summary: Founded in 1404 for Louis of Savoy-Acaja by the Avignon pope Benedict XIII, it wandered between Turin, Chieri and Savigliano. Victor Amadeus II's reform of 1720 made it the centralised state university of Savoy-Piedmont.
institutions.notes: Emmanuel Philibert's university at Mondovì (1560–66) is treated as a phase of Turin's.

institutions.name: Royal Schools of Artillery and Fortification
alt: Regie Scuole Teoriche e Pratiche di Artiglieria e Fortificazione
institutions.summary: Military engineering school of the Kingdom of Sardinia, one of the earliest in Europe. Lagrange taught mathematics there as a teenager.

institutions.name: Royal Veterinary School of Venaria
institutions.summary: Early veterinary school founded at Venaria Reale under Charles Emmanuel III, directed by Carlo Giovanni Brugnone; ancestor of Turin's veterinary school.
institutions.notes: Later moves to Turin are not recorded here.

institutions.name: Scuola di Applicazione per gli Ingegneri di Torino
institutions.summary: Engineering school created by the Casati law; it merged with the Museo Industriale to form the Politecnico di Torino in 1906.

institutions.name: Regio Museo Industriale
institutions.summary: Technical institute teaching industrial engineering, where Galileo Ferraris taught electrotechnics; merged into the Politecnico in 1906.

institutions.name: University of Genoa
institutions.summary: Degree-granting colleges of doctors authorised by the Genoese pope Sixtus IV in 1471, later joined by Jesuit teaching. After the 1773 suppression the Republic created a unified university in the former Jesuit college.
institutions.notes: Status before 1773 was a set of colleges plus the Jesuit college rather than a full university.

institutions.name: Regia Scuola Superiore Navale
institutions.summary: Higher school of naval architecture and marine engineering.

institutions.name: Jesuit College of Brera
institutions.summary: Jesuit college given the Brera complex by Carlo Borromeo, teaching philosophy and theology at university level. Its observatory (1764) and buildings passed to the state after 1773.

institutions.name: Veterinary School of Milan
institutions.summary: Veterinary school established by the Austrian government in Lombardy.
institutions.notes: Foundation date approximate.

institutions.name: Politecnico di Milano
institutions.summary: Founded as the Istituto Tecnico Superiore by Francesco Brioschi to train engineers and architects for Italian industry.

institutions.name: Regia Scuola Superiore di Commercio
institutions.summary: The first Italian higher school of commerce, housed in Ca' Foscari.

institutions.name: University of Macerata
institutions.summary: Communal law school from 1290, raised to studium generale by Paul III in 1540.

institutions.name: University of Camerino
institutions.summary: Small studium of the Varano lords' town, granted papal privileges in 1377 and refounded by Benedict XIII in 1727.

institutions.name: University of Urbino
institutions.summary: Founded as a degree-granting college of doctors under Guidobaldo da Montefeltro and recognised by Pius IV in 1564.

institutions.name: University of Fermo
institutions.summary: Granted a studium generale by Boniface VIII in 1303 and effectively refounded by Sixtus V in 1585; suppressed in the early 19th century.
institutions.notes: The 1303 grant appears to have been largely unrealised; end date uncertain.

institutions.name: University of Catania
institutions.summary: The first university of Sicily, founded by Alfonso V of Aragon, confirmed by Eugenius IV in 1444 and opened in 1445.

institutions.name: University of Messina
institutions.summary: Begun as the first Jesuit college with a papal bull of 1548, it became a municipal studium in 1596. Spain suppressed it after the revolt of 1674–78; it was restored in 1838.

institutions.name: Jesuit College of Palermo
institutions.summary: Jesuit college offering higher teaching in philosophy and theology until the expulsion of 1767.

institutions.name: University of Palermo
institutions.summary: Created from the Jesuits' former schools as the Royal Academy of Studies and raised to a university in 1805.

institutions.name: University of Cagliari
institutions.summary: Founded on the petition of the Sardinian parliament with Philip III's and Paul V's approval, opened in 1626 and refounded by Charles Emmanuel III of Savoy in 1764.

institutions.name: University of Sassari
institutions.summary: Born from a Jesuit college endowed by Alessio Fontana, recognised as a university in the 17th century and refounded by Savoy in 1765.

institutions.name: University of Corsica (Corte)
institutions.summary: University of Pasquale Paoli's independent Corsican Republic, closed after the French conquest.

institutions.name: Collegium Melitense
institutions.summary: Jesuit college in Valletta and precursor of the University of Malta.

institutions.name: University of Malta
institutions.summary: Founded by Grand Master Pinto from the former Jesuit college.

institutions.name: Scuola di Applicazione di Ponti e Strade
institutions.summary: Engineering school founded by Murat.

institutions.name: Collegio dei Cinesi
institutions.summary: Founded by Matteo Ripa to train Chinese missionaries; later the Istituto Orientale.

institutions.name: Scuola di Applicazione per gli Ingegneri di Roma
institutions.summary: Engineering school founded in Rome.

events.title: Conventional beginning of law teaching
events.desc: Teaching of Roman law by Pepo and Irnerius emerges spontaneously in Bologna; 1088 is the conventional date adopted in 1888.

events.title: Authentica Habita
events.desc: Frederick I Barbarossa's privilege (Roncaglia, 1155/1158) grants travelling scholars imperial protection and special jurisdiction, the founding charter of scholarly privilege.

events.title: Honorius III and the archdeacon's licence
events.desc: Pope Honorius III places the conferral of the licentia docendi under the archdeacon of Bologna, giving the doctorate an ecclesiastical sanction.

events.title: Ius ubique docendi
events.desc: Nicholas IV grants Bologna graduates the right to teach everywhere (ius ubique docendi), formally confirming its status as a studium generale.

events.title: Faculty of theology
events.desc: Innocent VI authorises a theological faculty, completing the university's full complement of faculties; the same year Cardinal Albornoz's Collegio di Spagna opens.

events.title: Archiginnasio
events.desc: Under Pius IV and the legate Carlo Borromeo the scattered schools are concentrated in the new Archiginnasio palace, a sign of tighter papal control.

events.title: Laura Bassi graduates
events.desc: Laura Bassi receives a doctorate in philosophy and a public lectureship, the first woman to hold a university chair in Europe.

events.title: Napoleonic national university
events.desc: Under the Italian Republic/Kingdom of Italy Bologna becomes one of the national universities; it moves to Palazzo Poggi and absorbs Marsili's Istituto delle Scienze.

events.title: Incorporation into Italy
events.desc: After the Papal Legations join Piedmont-Sardinia, the university is reorganised under the Casati law system of the new Italian state.

events.title: Secession from Bologna
events.desc: Masters and students leaving Bologna, apparently including the canonist Pillius's circle and others, begin teaching in Vicenza.

events.title: Roffredo leaves Bologna
events.desc: Roffredo Epifanio of Benevento and other Bolognese teachers begin teaching law in Arezzo.

events.title: Statutes of 1255
events.desc: The studium adopts statutes, among the oldest surviving university statutes in Italy.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV confirms Arezzo as a studium generale.

events.title: Secession from Bologna
events.desc: Bolognese students and masters migrate to Padua, founding a studium of law that soon adds arts and medicine.

events.title: Venetian takeover
events.desc: After Venice conquers Padua (1405) the Republic makes the studium its sole university and forbids subjects to study elsewhere (1407).

events.title: War of the League of Cambrai
events.desc: Teaching is suspended during the War of the League of Cambrai.

events.title: Reopening after Cambrai
events.desc: The Venetian Senate reopens the studium after the war.

events.title: Botanical garden
events.desc: The Orto botanico, the first university botanical garden, is founded; the permanent anatomical theatre follows in 1594.

events.title: Elena Cornaro Piscopia
events.desc: Elena Lucrezia Cornaro Piscopia receives a doctorate in philosophy, the first woman known to earn a university doctorate.

events.title: Napoleonic reorganisation
events.desc: Padua becomes a national university of the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy, with reorganised faculties.

events.title: Closure after 8 February 1848
events.desc: After clashes between students and Austrian troops on 8 February 1848 the university is closed by the Austrian authorities; teaching resumed only gradually.

events.title: Annexation to Italy
events.desc: With Venetia's annexation the university passes into the Italian system.

events.title: Contract with Paduan students
events.desc: The commune of Vercelli signs a contract with student rectors from Padua, promising lodgings, loans and salaried masters.

events.title: Communal studium
events.desc: A communal ordinance of 1240 records the commune paying masters and housing students, the first evidence of the studium.

events.title: Privileges of Innocent IV
events.desc: Pope Innocent IV grants masters and students exemptions and privileges.

events.title: Bolognese secession
events.desc: After a student is executed in Bologna, many masters and students move to Siena, which hires them and petitions for studium generale status.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV recognises Siena as a studium generale.

events.title: French closure
events.desc: Under French rule the university is closed.

events.title: Restoration reopening
events.desc: Grand Duke Ferdinand III reopens the university after the Restoration.

events.title: Tuscan university
events.desc: Leopold II unites Pisa and Siena into a single Tuscan university, leaving Siena mainly theology and law; autonomy is restored in 1859.

events.title: Foundation by Frederick II
events.desc: Frederick II's letter of 5 June 1224 founds the studium and forbids his subjects to study elsewhere.

events.title: Transfer to Salerno
events.desc: Conrad IV transfers the studium to Salerno.

events.title: Return to Naples
events.desc: Manfred restores the studium to Naples.

events.title: Angevin re-establishment
events.desc: Charles I of Anjou re-establishes and regulates the studium after his conquest.

events.title: Palazzo degli Studi
events.desc: Viceroy Lemos moves the university into the new Palazzo degli Studi.

events.title: Chair of political economy
events.desc: A chair of commerce and mechanics (political economy), funded by Bartolomeo Intieri, is created for Antonio Genovesi - the first of its kind in Europe.

events.title: Move to the former Jesuit college
events.desc: After the Jesuits' expulsion (1767) Ferdinand IV moves the university into the former Jesuit college of the Salvatore and reorganises studies.

events.title: French reorganisation
events.desc: Under Joseph Bonaparte and Murat the university is reorganised on French lines, with new chairs in sciences.

events.title: Bourbon reaction
events.desc: After the failed revolution of 1848 Ferdinand II purges liberal teachers and restricts university attendance in Naples.

events.title: Unification reform
events.desc: Francesco De Sanctis, as minister, reorganises the university, appointing new professors in the Italian system.

events.title: Emergence of Salernitan medicine
events.desc: Physicians of Salerno become renowned; no formal foundation act exists.

events.title: Constitutions of Melfi
events.desc: Frederick II requires that physicians in the Kingdom be examined by the masters of Salerno before licensing.

events.title: Angevin statutes
events.desc: Charles I of Anjou recognises Salerno as a studium generale of medicine.

events.title: Abolished by Murat
events.desc: Joachim Murat's reorganisation of public education closes the school.

events.title: Bull In supremae praeeminentia dignitatis
events.desc: Boniface VIII's bull of 20 April 1303 founds a studium generale for the city of Rome.

events.title: Eugenius IV
events.desc: Eugenius IV reorganises the studium and funds it from a tax on imported wine.

events.title: Union with the Studium Curiae
events.desc: The papal court's itinerant Studium Curiae is traditionally regarded as absorbed into the Studium Urbis in this period.

events.title: Sack of Rome
events.desc: Imperial troops sack Rome and teaching collapses for several years.

events.title: Sant'Ivo and the Alessandrina
events.desc: Alexander VII completes the Sapienza palace with Borromini's Sant'Ivo and founds the Biblioteca Alessandrina (1667).

events.title: Leo XII's reform
events.desc: The bull Quod divina sapientia reorganises all universities of the Papal States, with Rome and Bologna as primary universities.

events.title: Italian state takeover
events.desc: After the capture of Rome the university becomes a royal Italian university.

events.title: Theology faculty abolished
events.desc: The Italian state abolishes faculties of theology in state universities.

events.title: Bull of Innocent IV
events.desc: Innocent IV, at the Council of Lyon, establishes a studium of theology and law at the papal court.

events.title: Curia returns to Italy
events.desc: The studium returns with Innocent IV to Italy.

events.title: Avignon papacy
events.desc: The studium follows the papacy to Avignon.

events.title: Return to Rome
events.desc: The curia and its studium return to Rome under Gregory XI.

events.title: School opens
events.desc: Ignatius opens a free school of grammar, humanities and Christian doctrine near the Capitol on 22 February 1551.

events.title: Degree-granting powers
events.desc: Paul IV authorises the college to confer degrees in philosophy and theology.

events.title: Gregory XIII's new college
events.desc: Gregory XIII endows and builds a new college, inaugurated in 1584; hence the name 'Gregorian'.

events.title: Suppression of the Jesuits
events.desc: Clement XIV's brief Dominus ac Redemptor suppresses the Society; the college passes to secular clergy.

events.title: Returned to the Jesuits
events.desc: Leo XII restores the college to the re-established Society of Jesus.

events.title: Expelled by the Italian state
events.desc: The state confiscates the building; the college moves to Palazzo Borromeo and continues as the Pontifical Gregorian University.

events.title: Bull Immortalis Dei
events.desc: Urban VIII founds the college under the Congregation de Propaganda Fide.

events.title: Bull Super specula
events.desc: Clement V's bull of 8 September 1308 makes Perugia a studium generale.

events.title: Degrees in canon and civil law
events.desc: John XXII authorises degrees in civil and canon law (later extended to medicine and arts, 1321).

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV confirms the studium's privileges.

events.title: Leo XII's reform
events.desc: Under Quod divina sapientia Perugia becomes a secondary university of the Papal States.

events.title: Free university
events.desc: After annexation to Italy Perugia becomes a 'free' university financed by local bodies.

events.title: Charter of Frederick the Fair
events.desc: The German king Frederick the Fair grants Treviso the rights of a studium generale.

events.title: Bull of Clement VI
events.desc: Clement VI's bull In supremae dignitatis (3 September 1343) grants Pisa a studium generale.

events.title: Lorenzo's refoundation
events.desc: Lorenzo de' Medici re-establishes the studium in Pisa as the university of the Florentine state, transferring most of the Studio Fiorentino there.

events.title: Exile during the Pisan revolt
events.desc: With Pisa in revolt against Florence, the studio moves to Prato (and also Florence and Pistoia).

events.title: Return to Pisa
events.desc: Teaching resumes in Pisa after Florence reconquers the city.

events.title: Cosimo I
events.desc: Cosimo I restores the university with new chairs, the Sapienza building and the botanical garden (1544).

events.title: Napoleonic academy
events.desc: Under French rule Pisa becomes an Académie of the Imperial University and the Scuola Normale is founded.

events.title: Tuscan university
events.desc: Leopold II merges Pisa and Siena into one Tuscan university, partly in reprisal for the students' role in 1848; separated again in 1859.

events.title: Communal studium
events.desc: The Florentine commune resolves to found a studium, profiting from the Bolognese crisis.

events.title: Bull of Clement VI
events.desc: Clement VI grants studium generale status with a theology faculty.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV confirms the studium with imperial privileges.

events.title: Decree of the provisional government
events.desc: Bettino Ricasoli's government decrees the institute in December 1859.

events.title: Ernestina Paper graduates
events.desc: Ernestina Paper takes a medical degree, the first woman to graduate in united Italy.

events.title: Napoleonic decree
events.desc: Imperial decree of 18 October 1810 creates the school as a branch of the Paris École normale.

events.title: Fall of Napoleon
events.desc: The school lapses with the end of French rule.

events.title: Scuola Normale Toscana
events.desc: Grand Duke Leopold II re-establishes it as a Tuscan teacher-training school.

events.title: National Scuola Normale
events.desc: The Matteucci regulations make it the Scuola Normale Superiore of the Kingdom of Italy.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV's diploma of 13 April 1361 grants Pavia a studium generale at the request of Galeazzo II Visconti.

events.title: Bull of Boniface IX
events.desc: Boniface IX confirms the studium with papal privileges including theology.

events.title: Transfer to Piacenza
events.desc: Gian Galeazzo Visconti transfers the studium to Piacenza.

events.title: Return to Pavia
events.desc: Filippo Maria Visconti restores the studium to Pavia.

events.title: Theresian reform
events.desc: Maria Theresa's government reorganises the university with new statutes, buildings and chairs (1771–1773).

events.title: Austro-Russian closure
events.desc: The returning Austrians close the university.

events.title: Reopening after Marengo
events.desc: Napoleon's victory leads to the university's reopening; it becomes a national university of the Kingdom of Italy.

events.title: Casati law
events.desc: Lombardy's annexation brings Pavia under the Casati law of the Kingdom of Sardinia.

events.title: Bull of Innocent IV
events.desc: Innocent IV grants Piacenza the privileges of a studium generale.

events.title: Law teaching attested
events.desc: Masters of law are attested teaching in Reggio.

events.title: Pillius in Modena
events.desc: The jurist Pillius moves from Bologna to Modena and teaches law.

events.title: Francesco II d'Este
events.desc: Duke Francesco II d'Este establishes the public university.

events.title: Francesco III's constitutions
events.desc: Francesco III reforms the university with new constitutions and buildings.

events.title: Annexation to Italy
events.desc: The university passes into the Italian system after the fall of the Este duchy.

events.title: Niccolò III d'Este
events.desc: Niccolò III d'Este, then lord of Parma, founds a studium generale.

events.title: Ranuccio I Farnese
events.desc: Duke Ranuccio I Farnese re-establishes the university, entrusting part of it to the Jesuits.

events.title: Du Tillot's reform
events.desc: After the Jesuits' expulsion, Du Tillot reorganises the university as a state institution.

events.title: Bull of Boniface IX
events.desc: Boniface IX's bull of 4 March 1391 founds the studium generale.

events.title: Leonello d'Este
events.desc: Leonello d'Este re-establishes the studium after decades of decline.

events.title: Papal devolution
events.desc: With Ferrara's devolution to the Papal States the university passes under papal control.

events.title: Leo XII's reform
events.desc: Ferrara is classed as a secondary university under Quod divina sapientia.

events.title: Free university
events.desc: After unification Ferrara continues as a 'free' university funded by local bodies.

events.title: Bull of Benedict XII
events.desc: Benedict XII grants Verona the right to a studium generale.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Emperor Charles IV grants Cividale the rights of a studium generale.

events.title: Charter of Charles IV
events.desc: Charles IV grants Lucca a studium generale on freeing the city from Pisan rule.

events.title: Bull of Benedict XIII
events.desc: The Avignon pope Benedict XIII founds the studium (October 1404).

events.title: Charter of Sigismund
events.desc: Emperor Sigismund confirms the studium.

events.title: Move to Chieri
events.desc: The studium moves to Chieri.

events.title: Move to Savigliano
events.desc: The studium moves to Savigliano.

events.title: Return to Turin
events.desc: The studium returns to Turin.

events.title: Mondovì
events.desc: Emmanuel Philibert establishes the university at Mondovì while Turin is under French occupation.

events.title: Return to Turin
events.desc: The university returns to Turin.

events.title: Victor Amadeus II
